sgroppino.e: Etymology tree Italian sgroppinobor. English sgroppino Borrowed from Italian sgroppino.

sgabello.e: Etymology tree Italian sgabellobor. English sgabello Borrowed from Italian sgabello.

sgudal.e: Etymology tree Scottish Gaelic sgudalbor. English sgudal Borrowed from Scottish Gaelic sgudal.

Sgro.e: Borrowed from Sicilian Sgrò. Compare also Sicilian Sgroi and Isgrò.

sgian dubh.e: Borrowed from Scottish Gaelic sgian-dubh: sgian (“knife”) (ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *sek- (“to cut; to cut off, sever”)) + dubh (“black; (figurative) hidden”) (ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *dʰewbʰ- (“deep”)). The plural form sgianan dubha is also borrowed from Scottish Gaelic.

sglods.e: Unadapted borrowing from Welsh sglods, an alternative plural to Welsh sglodion (“chips”).
